During the day, trucks sometimes had a smaller 60-mph peak on freeways and distributed their time over speeds under 40 mph slightly more. Generally, we had less robust data and were thus less confident in results from rural roads and weekend data. 5.1.4 Combined FleetDNA and CE-CERT Speed Distributions for Source Type and Vocation by Day As shown in the previous sections, many hours of the day had insufficient data to estimate their own average speed distribution. Additionally, as discussed in Section 5.3, we did not observe meaningful trends in the average speed across hours of the day in the samples. For the combined database, we grouped data over all hours to calculate the average speed distributions by source type, road type, and day type using Equation 4. This larger level of aggregation lends more data to each speed distribution. We display an example output for transit buses on urban other roads on weekdays in Table 7.
